items.title: 68436_Alberta Hunter oral history interview
items.q: Well, Elgar's band -- he had a band I forget his first name -- Elgar, his musicians would come; everybody would come, all the musicians from the different places.

ctx.x: Lil told me that there were Chicago musicians, but they didn't really swing like --

They didn't play like those New Orleans boys did. The New Orleans boys had something that the Chicago musicians couldn't get at that particular time. And I tell you what. Every musician in the area that could get to the Dreamland would be there to come to sit in with those fellows to play, to try to get their style and see what they did, you know, and especially during the after hours. After hours they'd come and sit with those New Orleans musicians.

From all downtown, from everywhere they'd come from way over on the West side. They had a Dreamland over on the West side, you know, a dance place. Well, Elgar's band -- he had a band I forget his first name -- Elgar, his musicians would come; everybody would come, all the musicians from the different places.
